notes: Calendar categories, simpler: Family first, then your own groups (drag people in), then general categories – each with a colour you pick from a palette (or any colour). The Google Calendar colours are worked out for you; “Which colour to pick in Google Calendar” lists them
The calendar key: “as a line” is a tick box
Rewards and Advanced have a menu down the left – the first item explains the page, and each item opens on the right. No more clicking through pages
Morning to-dos and reminders: one compact line each, with the column names at the top

Calendar categories now use Google Calendar’s own event colours (on your main calendar): pick the colour on an event in Google Calendar or Gmail and it lands in that category. Up to 10 categories – family groups and general ones
Events for one person: Graphite, with their name in brackets at the end – “Drums (Ben)”. They show in that person’s colour, their group’s, or Family’s
Setup → Screens → a calendar page: the categories (drag people into groups), and that page’s own key – up to 9 plus Other, up to two shown as lines under each day, or hidden
“Tidy up your Google calendar”: lists events in the old “Ben – Drums” form, with no category or with titles too long, and fixes the ones you tick
Adding an event: pick General, a group or one person
Picking the Google calendar for a page from a list
Family: just the people, their colours and ⭐ Rewards
The Setup website, reorganised: Set up (First-time setup · Screens · Family · Rewards · Advanced) · Help · Apps (Calendar · Notes · Lists · Widgets)
Screens & widgets: a “How this works” page at the top of the screens list; at most 6 screens
Family: who’s in the family (up to 10), their colours, and ⭐ Rewards – with an explainer
Rewards: everything on one page – tasks, morning to-dos, reminders, rules, changing a child’s points by hand (add, take away, set the balance, statement) and each child’s card
Advanced: Settings (home & places, data keys, system) · My data · My devices · About & diagnostics
Calendar and Help open inside the website; with more than one calendar page you can switch between them
“Points” is now “Rewards”

Family tab in three parts: Family links and apps · Set up children’s points, tasks and reminders (Set up tasks, morning to-dos, reminders, points rules – each opens on its own) · Each child as they’ll show on the dashboard
Morning to-dos and reminders: one line each on a computer
The family’s Google calendars are set on the calendar page in Screen layout (not in Reconfigure → Family)
Setup → Screen layout: a calendar page’s settings sit under its picture – which Google calendars it shows, where new events go, what it opens on, lining up weekdays
You can have more than one calendar page, each showing different Google calendars (add one with “Add a screen” → Calendar)
Widgets tab: the children’s points widgets aren’t listed (they’re on the Family tab)
Setup → Family: four buttons at the top – Family Calendar (opens in a new tab), Today & tomorrow, Where is everyone and Reconfigure the family – then the children side by side with everything showing
Setup: the tabs are in two groups, “Set up” and “Everyday”
The holiday countdown’s settings are under Widgets
Holiday countdown: clearer help for “Your own dates” – one per line as name | date, e.g. Orlando | 3/4/2027, or Christmas | 25 Dec (no year) for one that comes round every year
Setup → Screen layout: clicking a widget shows how it appears (height, show, when to show, remove) on the left and its own settings on the right, saved together – no page picker (drag it instead)
A widget shown in place of another at other times opens straight to its own settings
Each copy of a widget has its own settings. A new copy starts with the first one’s settings; removing a spare copy drops its settings; removing the last one keeps them for next time

Child points widgets, rearranged for at-a-glance: name, reminders, points with the Cash in button beside them, three next tasks, this morning – then the progress bar and penalty buttons at the bottom. Drag up and down to scroll if there’s more

The screen gets itself going again: if the Sheet hasn’t answered for 10 minutes and nobody is using it, it reloads itself (then after 20, 40 and every 60 minutes if still stuck) – only when it can load its own page, so it never ends up on a “no internet” page
Today & tomorrow: days on the left (Today above Tomorrow), the weekend on the right; with only two, side by side
Setup → Screen layout: a widget split by “When to show” is all you need – click either half for its settings; the hidden copy that holds the other widget’s settings isn’t listed any more
Setup → Screen layout: a newly added widget shows “Adding…” and its standard settings straight away (no more “undefined”)
Flights overhead: if adsb.lol is busy (“said 429”) it uses airplanes.live instead, by itself
Setup → Connect this computer: the picture above the title shows again
The screen’s “Try the Sheet again” button now says what happened: “Connected – the Sheet answered at 08:40”, or why it still can’t

When the screen can’t reach the Sheet it now tells you which kind of problem it is: this PC can’t reach the internet/Google at all, or Google answered with an error (the script stopped or needs approving)

Children are now widgets: each child’s points card is a full-height widget you can put on any screen (four fit on one). Your points page has been turned into a screen of child widgets in the same place – move them about in Setup → Screen layout
A new child (Family & calendar → ⭐ Points) gets a widget of their own; renaming a child keeps theirs, and taking a child off points removes it (their points are kept)
Setup → Screen layout: no separate points screen to add any more – drag “Child (points)” from the widget list instead

Setup → Screen layout: a 🗑 on each widget, and a bin to drag widgets onto, to remove them; removing (from there or the widget’s own box) happens straight away, and a “won’t fit” box disappears as soon as it’s empty

Setup → Screen layout: widgets that don’t fit are shown underneath, ready to drag elsewhere or click to remove; calendar and points screens are drawn at the same size (without your data), and the points screen explains that extra screens are added for more children
Setup → Reconfigure opens each page on its own (no step list), with “Back to Setup”
The Family tab has a “Reconfigure the family” link – on the phone it points to Setup
Connect by code: after sending, Family Admin checks the screen or computer actually picked it up, and says so – or tells you to check the code

Setup website: tabs along the top – First-time setup, Screen layout, Reconfigure, Settings, then Family, Notes, Lists and Widgets. A computer that isn’t connected yet gets a choice: first-time setup, or connect this computer

The licence email and setup explain in plain English how it works (your data stays in your own Google account, reached only with your private access code) and what each step does, including what an API key is
Family Admin is described as for adults
Notes: up to 6, shown two at a time on the screen with “Page 1 of 3”, turning by themselves every 8 seconds (tap the page number to turn now)
Family Admin: the Memos tab is now Notes, showing the notes as they look on the screen, with a box to add one underneath
The Google script now checks GitHub for a newer version itself every few minutes, the same way as the “Update now” button, and the Updates page shows when it last checked and what happened
The screen retries a script update quietly every 3 minutes, instead of asking you to update by hand

Family Admin → Widgets: hidden widgets are listed too, and a “Not in use” section has the settings of every widget that isn’t on a screen. Removing a widget keeps its settings; adding it again brings them back
Family Admin: Settings → Updates is back on the phone, with “Update the Google script now” if it hasn’t updated itself
Family Admin: separate Memos and Lists tabs, and the Other tab is now called Widgets

The website for computers is now called Setup, at one address – russm1981.github.io/family-apps/setup – with first-time setup, every step-by-step guide, the screen layout and the rarer settings. Old links (licence emails, the Sheet’s menu, …/settings) still work

Settings website: a drag-and-drop screen layout editor – screens down the left (add widget, calendar or points screens), widgets to drag in on the right, and a preview as on the Corsair, a tablet or a computer. Widgets with “When to show” are drawn split diagonally with their times
Settings website: a Setup & tools tab with every guided step (family & calendar, connecting devices, keys, licence, check everything, updates, starting again)
The home page shows the three places: the dashboard, Family Admin (phone) and the settings website (computer)

Family Admin on the phone is for everyday use: points, lists, notes, the calendar and each widget’s everyday settings. The screen layout and rare settings (family & calendar set-up, places, API keys, updates, your Google data, diagnostics) are on the new settings website for a computer: russm1981.github.io/family-apps/settings
Tablets connect with a short address and a code typed on the computer – no long link to scan; setup’s QR codes are bigger and easier to scan
When to show: picking a widget for other times adds a hidden one to hold its settings if there isn’t one, and it can’t be removed while it’s in use; the list says which is which
Adding a widget shows straight away in Family Admin
Setup: after Deploy, copy the Web app URL and paste it into the setup page to connect – no Sheet menu needed
Setup and help: what to do if Deploy just spins or Google keeps asking for permission
Family Admin: moving widgets and pages happens instantly, and saved changes show straight away while they’re saved in the background – several quick taps are all kept, in order
Changes to the screen layout save much faster
When to show: times are picked from a list (no colon needed)
New Sheets: the Family Dashboard menu has “▶ Set up & connect my screen and phones” straight away (loader 1.2), and setup explains what to do if the menu only says “Load the dashboard program”
Fixes from a full review: QR codes in setup and on the home page no longer depend on an outside website
Today & tomorrow on a tablet: the weekend list is one column so names aren’t cut short; a repeating event on Saturday and Sunday shows on both days
When to show: times are checked properly (24-hour clock, 24:00 for midnight)
When to show: the widget shown at other times has to be the same height (half with half, full with full)
Any widget can show only on certain days and times, with another widget in its space the rest of the time (Family Admin → Screen → the widget → When to show)
Trains: disruption messages only about your route, all of them, or off
Today & tomorrow: something on both days of the weekend is labelled ALL
Today & tomorrow: the weekend is grouped under one heading with each entry’s day – “This weekend” Monday to Thursday, in place of tomorrow on Fridays, and “Next weekend” on Saturdays and Sundays
Family Calendar and Family Admin say clearly when a licence key is needed, with a box to type it in, instead of just not loading
Today & tomorrow: up to 3 things a day, with the coming weekend’s Saturday and Sunday underneath
Setup is clearer for a new family: an overview of the steps, every click spelled out, its own licence key step, and a warning if it’s opened on a phone
The licence email explains exactly what to do and opens setup with the key already in it
The screen’s “Add your licence key” page lets you type the key in on the screen itself

Every app shows which family it’s connected to and can be disconnected: Family Calendar (⚙ next to Today), Family Admin (Settings → Devices → This phone), the screen (Status page), the setup app and the home page
Connecting a screen from a phone now says whose dashboard it will show and asks “Is this screen in your home?” – with “No – it’s someone else’s screen” leading to their own setup
Screen status page: “Disconnect this screen”
A copy of someone else’s dashboard Sheet is emptied automatically before anything is shown; Sheet menu “Clear everything and start from scratch”

Bins simplified: one place to set them up (Set up bin days); the settings only hold the reminder time; the council is shown plainly with “Not right?” instead of a long list; by hand (with the AI helper) is the clear next step when a council can’t be read
Google script 2026.11.35

Bins by hand: “Let an AI assistant look it up” – a ready-written request (with your postcode, house and council) to copy into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini; paste its answer back and your bins are filled in
Bins: Dorset Council can now be read automatically (13 councils)
Google script 2026.11.34

Bins: “Set up bin days” in Family Admin – postcode → your council (change it if wrong) → read automatically where we can (12 councils so far, more being added), otherwise a simple form to enter your bins by hand, with a preview
Diagnostics: when a widget (or setting up bin days) fails, the report now includes what was asked of the outside service and what came back – in the locked part
Google script 2026.11.33

Family Admin and Family Calendar on a computer: connect by typing the code they show into your phone (Family Admin → Settings → Devices → Connect by code), or scan their QR code – no links to copy; if the browser already has another app connected, one tap uses the same family
Home page: “Connect this browser” the same way – it then shows your own links and settings
Calendar Year view is now a wall planner: a row for each month (all 12 when there’s room), lined up by weekday or not – the same setting as the 3-month views
Calendar key: along the bottom on a tablet (except Month view, where it stays on the right), and small along the bottom in Year view on a computer; the Corsair is unchanged
Tablets and computers no longer use the dashboard’s sleep screen – the tablet’s power button or the computer’s own settings do that; the Corsair keeps it
Tablets: the first tap makes the dashboard full screen; it can also be added to the home screen and opens full screen from there
Tablet: side bar shows icons only, with 1 and 2 on pages split in two; a proper calendar icon showing today’s date
Tablet calendar: the key runs along the bottom and the month names take less room, so the days get the full width
Tablet children’s page: each child’s card scrolls when there’s more than fits (the morning list was cut off)
Browser tab says “Family Dashboard”
Family Admin → Family: the calendar and family tiles come first, then the points cards – each child now has its own “Set up points” link
Family Admin → Settings → System → Licence shows your whole licence key once it’s been entered, with a Copy button
Google script 2026.11.32
Setup is simpler: no Apps Script API switch – publish once with Deploy → New deployment, and the script keeps itself up to date
Fewer Google permissions: the script no longer asks to manage Apps Script projects and deployments
Google script 2026.11.31

Google script and licence server now run through a small loader that fetches the newest program each time: updates arrive within 5 minutes with no Apps Script API, no Google Cloud project and no saved versions used. Paste Loader.gs in once.
Google script 2026.11.30 · licence server 2026.11.12
Automatic updates: when Google’s Apps Script API is off in a script’s own Google Cloud project, the message now gives the project and a direct link to switch it on (the apps show an “Enable” button)
Licence server 2026.11.11: clears old “update failed” notes once it’s up to date

Tablets: each widget page with more than two columns gets two buttons in the side bar (e.g. Home 1, Home 2) instead of swiping and turning over by itself
Children’s page: 3 children a screen on the Corsair and computers, 2 on a tablet, with as many buttons as needed (Boys 1, Boys 2…); on a tablet it now fills the screen's height

Family Admin tabs: Family (points with your controls, calendar, today & tomorrow, holidays) · Lists · Other (information first: bins, weather, trains, buses, traffic) · Screen (where widgets go and how tall) · Settings
Each widget’s settings are on its own page; the Screen tab is only for layout – one layout for the Corsair, tablets and computers

Phone apps left open check for updates (on opening, when brought back to the front, and every 15 minutes) and restart themselves – or show “Update ready – Restart” if you’re in the middle of something

Family Admin settings reorganised: Family & calendar · Locations & home · External data (API) keys · System · My data (Google) · Devices · About & diagnostics · Help

My data (Google): go through setup again with everything filled in, start afresh, start from scratch, move to another Google account, access code
Bins work anywhere in the UK: from your council where connected, your council’s calendar (iCal) link, or a repeating schedule – with a clear message if your council isn’t connected
